He assesses that Uber Black pricing can avoid price-sensitive competition that compresses margins.
Charles asks about repeat usage and whether the service can become habitual.
Charles probes whether the company consists of distinct service models, separating accompanied from unaccompanied pet transport.
He states that Uber may be able to provide the accompanied pet ride easily, indicating limited differentiation in that segment.
Charles identifies unaccompanied pet transport to the vet as a separate service component.
Charles explicitly conditions his decision on whether the accompanied pet ride becomes commoditized and whether the remaining business is still interesting.
He sees potential for substantially higher pricing on accompanied pet visits, but treats it as an unresolved possibility.
Charles says he needs conviction that the business can remain attractive if the basic service becomes more commoditized or competitive.
His pass is tied to uncertainty about which higher-end offerings are difficult for competitors to replicate.
Charles believes higher-end service models may produce an interesting company, while seeking further evidence before investing.
